items.author: rme33.bsky.social
items.context: This is another reason why I almost always wait to buy AAA games until they have completed their updates and DLC, at which point I wait for a sale and get it all for the same price as, and often less than, the base game originally cost. This is one way to ensure publishers profit less off add-ons.
items.text: Waiting for the complete edition is a solid plan. Checking the game's price history before you buy helps you spot a real low.

items.author: thisisfineg.bsky.social
items.context: What we all playing today??? Surprise, I’ll probably do more Control 2, near the end so we’ll see if I can finish, but I kinda wanna play something a lil shorter after it! I’ll check mi steam library and check for shorter spooky games! 😂🎃☠️
items.text: A short spooky game after a long one sounds like a perfect palate cleanser. Sorting your Steam library by hours played is a quick way to dig out the ones you never started. 🎃

items.author: matthewoldfield.bsky.social
items.context: They're stuck because discretionary income is shrinking. Increase price ppl will wait for sales or buy and play older games. I already do that. I buy a new game once or twice a year (that's also because I have kids and don't game as much)
items.text: Older games are great value, a lot of them hold up really well. Adding them to your Steam wishlist makes it easy to catch a sale when it comes.

items.author: yvetterose.bsky.social
items.context: I go home from work in a little over an hour and I still haven't decided on what game I'm playing tonight 😭🥴 It's so funny how something always happens when I want to play XIV and it goes down lmao. Maybe an RPG tonight, but I can't decide on which one to focus 🤔
items.text: Servers going down right when you want to play is the worst. If you go with an RPG tonight, one you can drop into for a short session is a nice backup for nights like this.
